name: @helm/desktop
description: Helm's Electron shell: main process, preload, renderer.
//productName: Electron derives app.getName() - and therefore %APPDATA%\<name> - from this file. Without productName a scoped package name puts the database in %APPDATA%\@helm/desktop, creating a nested folder from the scope. electron-builder sets the same value for packaged builds.
author: Cole Taylor

scripts.//dev: --watch is what makes the main process and preload reload too. Without it electron-vite only gives the renderer HMR, and every main-process edit needs the app killed and restarted by hand.
scripts.//design-shot: Not a check. Opens the real window, walks the main views, and screenshots each in both themes - evidence for a design review against docs/DESIGN.md.
scripts.//m2-check: M2's acceptance criteria, driven through the real app window. Spawns real claude sessions and ends them; see src/main/m2check.ts.
scripts.//m3-check: M3's acceptance criteria. Builds a profile through the real form, launches it, and asks the live session whether the composition worked. Three phases, orchestrated by run-m3.mjs rather than by && because node-pty's teardown loses the exit code; the report is the verdict. Pass --only=compose|fixture|shims through to re-run one group.
scripts.//m4-check: M4's acceptance criteria. Drives the session-history pane through the real window and checks every count against an independent read of ~/.claude/history.jsonl. Spawns two real claude sessions - one resumed through the app, one on its own pty to prove the index notices a session Helm did not start - so it takes minutes. Verdict is in m4-report.json; run-m4.mjs exists for the same reason run-m3.mjs does.
scripts.//m5-check: M5's acceptance criteria. Drives the config console through the real window: browses every scope against an independent readdir walk, edits a file in each and restores it hash-verified, adds an MCP server through the UI, then launches a real claude session and asks it whether the effective view predicted what it actually sees. Spawns one claude session on haiku, so it takes minutes. Pass --only=browse|edit|snapshot|json|external|mcp|effective|doctor to re-run one group.
scripts.//m6-check: M6's acceptance criteria. Opens every markdown file in the user's harness vault through the real window and checks the DOM it produced against a regex read of the same source, navigates a wikilink, interrogates the artifact frame's sandbox from inside it, measures search latency and scroll frame intervals, and edits a real note through the split editor with a hash-verified restore. Spawns no claude sessions, so it takes about a minute. Pass --only=browse|render|links|artifact|search|edit|scroll to re-run one group.
scripts.//m7-check: M7's acceptance criteria, in three phases. Phase 1 audits this checkout for personal paths (having first planted one to prove the auditor catches it) and checks the CLI Helm would launch against an independent 'where.exe' read. Phase 2 is a second app started with PORTABLE_EXECUTABLE_DIR pointed at a temp directory - the app's own portable-mode mechanism used as isolation - so first run happens against an empty database and an absent .claude without touching the real ones: it adds plain folders, scaffolds a harness and launches a real session from it, exercises the repos: key, converts a folder in place, and points the version guard at a stub CLI reporting 9.9.9. Phase 3 builds the artefacts if they are missing, runs the portable exe from a path with spaces, installs the NSIS package silently as the current user, runs the selftest out of the installed app, and uninstalls. Pass --only=audit|cli|firstrun|harness|scan|version|package to re-run one group.
scripts.//usage-check: The status bar's usage figures. Drives the real window: checks the painted percentages against its own JSON.parse of ~/.claude.json, watches a rewritten fixture reach the bar with no restart, lets a usage window roll over underneath the segment, points the reader at six broken readings and proves each paints nothing, measures the bar at four widths in both themes, measures the full transcript parse it avoids, and finally asks a live claude for /usage and compares. Pass --only=<groups> to re-run one group; the group list is the GROUPS const in src/main/usagecheck.ts, which is the only authority for it.
scripts.//settings-check: M8, M9 and M10's settings. Drives the settings pane through the real window: opens it from the title bar gear, points the CLI setting at a stub program and clears it again, adds two scan roots and removes one - checking the removal against the next scan's project set rather than against the list - flips the theme and reads back the colour Electron was handed for the window controls, sets the usage mode and confirms it on the status bar, clicks both quick accessors and watches the pane follow, and hand-sends a malformed write for every key after proving a valid one lands. Every UI assertion sits beside this driver's own read-only connection to the database file. Two phases, orchestrated by run-settings.mjs: the driver parks the settings it changed and a second app start reads them back and restores the originals. The terminal group (M9) spawns one claude session and nothing else does: the font and cursor claims are about live terminals in both registries, and only a session puts one in the session registry. The github group (M10) points ghPath at a gh that is installed and not signed in, which is the only honest way to see the 'run gh auth login' sentence on a machine whose real gh is signed in, and sets the polling interval through the pane including the 0 that disarms the timer. Pass --only=pane|claude|roots|appearance|accessors|validation|terminal|github to re-run one group.
scripts.//pr-check: M10, M11 and M12's pull-request surface. Four of its five phases answer from a gh this repo wrote - scripts/fake-gh.mjs behind a .cmd shim, aimed at the service with pointGh - because a pull request whose title changes between two passes, an authentication that fails and a payload that is not JSON are not things a real repository can be made to do on demand. The fixture is mutated underneath the same comparison before its clean pass is believed. Beside every claim about the pane there is a read the driver makes for itself: its own JSON.parse of the fixture, its own read-only connection to helm.db, its own git and its own gh. The review phase spawns real claude sessions and closes them; the checkout phase runs a real gh pr checkout in a real git repository in a path with a space and reads the branch back out of git. The live phase runs the real gh once against a repository it found by walking the scan roots itself, and skips out loud when the machine has no gh, no sign-in or nothing open. It borrows the real database and puts the settings back; run-prcheck.mjs restores them too if the driver dies first. Pass --only=fixture|detail|review|degrade|live to re-run one group.
scripts.//dist:win: Goes through scripts/dist-win.mjs rather than calling electron-builder directly. electron-builder resolves pnpm with which(), which prefers pnpm.EXE over pnpm.CMD on Windows; a stale standalone pnpm shadowing the managed one makes it either fail outright or - worse - fall back to the npm collector and silently produce artefacts with no app.asar.unpacked, which is an exe that cannot dlopen better-sqlite3. The wrapper checks the resolved pnpm answers the declared version and shims it for the child process if not.
scripts.//verify:artifact: Asserts a built exe actually carries app.asar.unpacked, by unwrapping the NSIS artefact and the app-64.7z nested inside it. Checking dist-app/win-unpacked instead would be checking electron-builder's scratch directory rather than the file a person downloads. With no arguments it checks every Helm-*.exe in dist-app; the release workflow names the two it is about to upload. Needs 7-Zip, which ships on the windows-latest runner image.
scripts.//icon: Draws build/icon.* and packs build/icon.ico. The .ico is committed, so this is not part of the build - run it when the artwork changes.

//electron: Pinned exactly, not a range. electron-builder downloads platform binaries for one specific release and refuses to guess which - a caret here fails the packaging step outright (electron-builder 26.15.3). It is also the right shape regardless: the packaged app must ship the runtime the drivers measured against.
